utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon everybody in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-03-69-T. The Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Registrar, I was just about to ask you to call the case, but that's done already. I have a few procedural matters and I was informed that there may be some procedural matters raised by the parties as well. Let's see to what extent the one covers the other. First of all, the Chamber has received a medical report today by Dr. Eekhof. The Chamber is pleased to hear, Mr. Stanisic, that compared to last week, you at least feel considerably better. That's on the record. The second item -- for the next item we have to move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to raise an issue about the medical situation. I don't know if it's a convenient time. I can wait, it's of no consequence to the Defence if we wait.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we first go through the matters I have on my list then you have an opportunity. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. I would like to inform the parties that the week of the 16th to the 20th of August will be a non-sitting week in this case. So that's the first week after the recess which we will not sit in that week. I put the following on the record: The Prosecution has sought to have proposed 65 ter 5183 which is an article of a medical journal to be added to the 65 ter list. On the 9th of June, 2010, the OTP has informally communicated to the Chamber that it withdraws the request to seek addition to the 65 ter list for this medical journal article, as I said, proposed 65 ter number 5183. Last matter that I would like to put on the record is that on the 9th of June of 2010, the Chamber has informally granted Dr. de Man's request to submit his next report later this month. He had asked for some delay. These were the matters I had on my agenda. Mr. Jordash, there was a matter you would like to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. It's in relation to Mr. Stanisic's illness but specifically in relation to a matter which is before Your Honours which is the matter of whether the Defence ought to be given access to Mr. Stanisic's medical records. And I apologise if it's trampling on matters which are probably before Your Honours but we would ask in the -- we would ask a decision if at all possible be made as soon as possible, and if I may just outline quickly why that is. Number one, Mr. Stanisic has, to a large degree, come into conflict with his treating doctor, Dr. Falke, and to a large extent has lost confidence in what Dr. Falke does for Mr. Stanisic. In our submission that is not unusual. It's not unusual that a patient falls out with his doctor. What is unusual in this situation is that Mr. Stanisic can do nothing really about that because his legal representatives do not have access to his medical records and cannot advocate on his behalf concerning the treatment. In an ordinary situation with an accused who is not incarcerated, he could change doctors or he could give his medical records to whoever he sought to have advocate on his behalf, in this situation, Mr. Stanisic is without any recourse because it is he himself doesn't have his medical records and neither do we. And secondly, in relation to this issue, we in the Defence would like to have those medical records because we feel hampered in making decisions about what work we can do with Mr. Stanisic in the Defence centre. Last week was a good example of that. Whilst Your Honours may take the view we could go through our MO, that, in our submission, is in a situation like what arose last week, not a very effective way of us being able to do our job. We would have to put questions to the RMO through the Trial Chamber, the Prosecution would have an opportunity to respond and so on and so forth. We would like to see the medical records that we can make decisions on a day-to-day as to what we can and cannot do with Mr. Stanisic in the detention centre. I apologise again for raising the issue because it is before Your Honours but nonetheless we are in a difficult situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there are, I think, several aspects of this matter. The first is the patient/doctor relationship and access to medical information. That is one. Primary responsibility for the medical care is in the hands of the Registry. And the second issue is reporting to the Chamber which is not without reason, not done by the treating physician but by reporting medical officers, we have separated that for good purposes, I would say. That's the second issue. Have you taken up the matter with the Registrar?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, no, because there is some confusion, and I had a lengthy discussion with our team about this. With the matter going before Your Honours in the Registry submission of the 14th of December of 2009 and our response on the 18th of December, 2009, we thought on one view it was a matter now before Your Honours. On the other hand, we recognize that the Registry might be a suitable avenue to go down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'll now have to review that. I hope you'll forgive me, perhaps that's different than my colleagues that I have not a recollection -- a reliable recollection at this moment on exactly what we said in December 2009. We'll further look into the matter, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Anything else? There is one matter which is related to the next witness to be called and that is recently filed 92 ter motion. We have not received responses yet which doesn't come as a surprise because the motion was filed rather late. Are there any observations by the Defence. Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We did not submit our written response. However, given that we are expecting the witness to enter by your leave, we wanted to put our position to you concerning the requested modality of taking this testimony. I believe this may be the best moment to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Simatovic Defence objects to the request for this witness to testify under Rule 92 ter. First of all, concerning the request itself made by the Prosecutor, this witness figures as a -- has been known as a viva voce witness, if not a few years. Only a few days back it was requested that his type of testimony be changed. It was not explained why, only certain general explanations were given and some limited legal argumentation. Other than that, no reasons were provided why the Prosecutor after so much time wished for this type of testimony to be changed. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Ms. Marcus, in order to not lose time, would you pay especially attention to avoiding repetitious evidence which is already in the statement or in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness JF-048. Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you give evidence, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require that you make solemn declaration the text of which is now handed out to you by the usher. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I shall speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Witness JF-048. Witness, we will call you JF-048 because protective measures are in place. The public will not see your face and will not use your name, although your testimony will be for to some extent in public and only where the evidence would be at risk to reveal your identity, the parties will ask for private session. You will first now be examined by Ms. Marcus, Ms. Marcus is counsel for the Prosecution, and you find her to your right. Ms. Marcus, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, JF-048.

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I ask the Court Officer please to call up 65 ter 5362, which is the witness's pseudonym sheet, but not to broadcast it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I ask you please to take a look at what we see on the screen in front of us. Where it says "witness name," is that your name?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Yes, that's my name.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Directing your attention to where it says "date of birth," is that your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Yes, that's my date of birth.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could we kindly go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, with your leave I would like to tender this pseudonym sheet in to evidence under seal, please, that's 65 ter number 5362.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, the number will be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number will be Exhibit P522, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P522 is admitted into evidence under seal. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: JF-048, do you recall giving a statement in this case on the 5th and 6th of May of the year 2000?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And do you recall testifying in the Milosevic case?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I request private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: JF-048, prior to coming to testify today did you have an opportunity to review the prior evidence you gave?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: You made a few corrections to your prior statement in proofing and I'd like to show you the proofing note which resulted.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could the Court Officer please call up 65 ter 5343. This is the proofing note, but please not to broadcast it. It is dated 13th of June, 2010.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: JF-048, is this document the product of the corrections you made during our preparations for your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Could we please zoom in. I'm unable to read it. Thank you. Yes, these are the corrections.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to review this proofing note prior to signing it?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, having reviewed your prior evidence including this proofing note, now apart from the corrections you made in this proofing note, is there anything else you would like to change?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: If you were to be asked the same questions today as you were asked when you gave your prior evidence, would you provide the same answers in substance?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: In essence I would. It's been a long time since these events and perhaps I wouldn't use the very same words, but the gist of my statement is the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now that you have taken the solemn declaration, do you affirm the accuracy and truthfulness of your prior evidence including the proofing note?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time the Prosecution tenders 65 ter 5346, 65 ter 5347, and 65 ter 5343 into evidence under seal. All three of them under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could you please assign numbers. 5346 and 5347 should be MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. 65 ter 5346 will be P523 marked for identification. 65 ter 5347 will be P524 marked for identification. And 65 ter 5343 will be P525, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The last one, the proofing note does not refer in any way to Kosovo, so, therefore, could we not yet already admit into evidence 5343. Although if the others are not admitted or at least if not major portions are admitted, it would lose its meaning. 5343 is admitted into evidence under seal. And the MFI'd documents should be under seal as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time I would also tender the nine related exhibits. With your leave, I'll just read the 65 ter numbers into the record, if that's how Your Honours wish to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, is it 65 ter 5348 up to and including 5355?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: With respect, Your Honours, it's up to 5356. This was due to the -- their being out of order in the ERN range, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see. Yes, I see that the last two are not in range. So, therefore, it's 5348 up to and including 5356. Any objections? (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The 65 ter number 5348 up until 5346, Your Honours, will be Exhibit P526 till Exhibit P534, Your Honours. All under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P526 up to and including P534 are admitted into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. May I place on the record now that the page reference that Your Honours queried before should be 14668 instead of 14688. I do apologise sincerely for the typographical error.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Pursuant to the Trial Chamber's instructions on the 18th of February, 2010, I will now read out a public summary of your evidence. This summary does not constitute evidence in this case. It is for the purpose of informing the public of the general nature of the evidence you have been called to present. To allay any concerns you may have about your security, this public summary will not contain any identifying information. JF-048 joined the group of the Serbian MUP known as the JATD or Red Berets in 1995. Over the course of the following year, he was sent to various Red Beret JATD camps. During his time at these sites and through his membership in the Red Berets under the Serbian DB, he became familiar with the structure of command within the Red Berets under the state security. He was present at a ceremony opening one of the camps in which both accused Stanisic and Simatovic were present. While at one of the training camps he was sent to, the witness became aware of the supplying of groups operating in the area. These other groups included Arkan's Men with both Arkan and Legija personally visiting the camp to obtain supplies and Boca's detachment who drove jeeps with scorpions on the sides who also came to this training camp to obtain supplies and ammunition. In addition, the witness saw the accuse Simatovic arrive at one of the camps, more than one of the camps, correction, in a helicopter in order to test new weapons. The witness will testify to the command structure in the camps and in his unit. JF-048 will identify his instructors, many of whom moved with the unit from one training camp to another along with the witness. At another camp the witness discovered about 30 prisoners who had had their sentences reduced for joining the war front. These prisoners acted like reservists to the Red Berets. JF-048 was present when the accused Simatovic stated that the witness's unit had to do whatever that was asked of them and also heard Simatovic make other statements as well. JF-048 will testify that unlike other branches of the state security service that had an official hierarchical organisational structure according to the MUP regulations, it was his perception that the Red Berets did not operate according to the official MUP DB rules. His perception was that his unit of the Red Berets reported directly through Dragoslav Krsmanovic to Franko Simatovic who JF-048 understood to be reporting to Stanisic and/or to Milosevic. That ends the public summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: JF-048, can you explain why you chose to join the unit?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: From your perspective, JF-048, when you joined the unit, what was your understanding of what unit you were joining?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: At that time the only thing I knew was what we had been told and that is that it was a special unit of the state security sector. We were also told that we were to undergo very rigorous training and that the background checks to join the unit were very stringent. A sentence remains as to my memory, it went something along the lines, it is very difficult to join this unit but it is even more difficult to leave it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: At the time you joined, did you know this unit to be the Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Specifically none of the instructors or the persons who appeared at location number 1 at that time did say we were the Red Berets. They did wear red berets, however. Of course, there were also rumours going around at location 1 that they were from the Red Berets. However, officially it was a special unit of the public security sector, of the state security sector, interpreter's correction, and this is what we were told.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: For the record I'm seeking clarification and elaboration of the witness's comments on pages 4 and 5 of his statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: One more question on this, JF-048. At this time that you joined, did you know that unit that you joined to be the JATD?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I can only say with certainty that it was a special unit of the state security sector. As for the acronym JATD, figured only later, at least that's how I remember it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: When you say later, can you tell us either a time-period or perhaps a location where you first came to understand that the group was the JATD?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: What I can remember specifically is that when our superiors told us that officially as of that day we were the anti-terrorist operations unit of the state security sector, and the official recognition took place a few months after that at location 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm conscious of the time. If Your Honours are sticking to the original schedule, this might be a good pausing point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll have a break and we'll resume at five minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: JF-048, as you are aware, your prior statement and testimony are now before the Chamber, so the questions I'm asking you are just follow-ups and clarifications on some of your prior evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I ask the Court Officer please to call up P528. This is one of the related exhibits that was admitted. It was 65 ter 5350.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, since they are all under seal, they should not be shown to the public.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: JF-048, this document is already in evidence. I just want to ask you one question about it. I note that on this document there is no mention of the JATD. Do you have any idea why?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: My opinion is that the JATD is not being referred to in this document because we were from the very beginning told very clearly that the unit was of an extremely secretive character and that we were strictly forbidden to discuss the operations of the unit and the very existence of that very unit. And this decision explains that I was to be employed by the state security sector, and that was the only thing that was required to be contained in that decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have an English text for those who are watching the English versions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you may.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: In your statement you say that the Red Berets were a kind of paramilitary branch of the DB. You talk about this a few times in your statement on pages 4 and 5. Can you explain what you meant when you said that?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: First and foremost, I graduated at location 1. I was in company of trainers, instructors, professors and taught by them. However, during those three years of education at location 1, there have never been actions by instructors or management personnel the likes of which occurred within the unit, and this first alerted me and my doubts. Later on at location 2, we were paid in cash for awhile without signing any chits as would be customary by regular employees of the Ministry of the Interior either to their bank accounts or on the basis of a form with an official seal of the ministry. We were paid in cash and this caused doubts among my colleagues and me, and we were looking at each other saying what is this, what is going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you explain a little more why, what kinds of doubts this caused being paid in cash, and maybe you could explain a little bit further as to what that made you doubt?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Well, when we came to location 2, several months intervened before we received official decisions on our employment with the Ministry of the Interior. We were official graduates from the secondary school at location 1. I don't want to mention any names. And my peers expected when being employed by the state organ that the first thing would be the written decision on employment and other supporting documents that were supposed to be produced pursuant to administrative roles. But nothing of sort materialised and this is what brought about our doubts. For instance, one of my school colleagues, several days after joining the unit, started doubting and he said I want to leave this outfit and he left the unit within a few days. There were some other cases later on which I can explain further if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did any of your commanders ever say anything which suggested to you that you were part of a secret unit as you've described to us?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Not once. My instructors kept on emphasising that we were not supposed to talk about the unit at home without -- to our friends, family, what we were doing, where we were at, and it has been emphasised on numerous occasions that this unit was a very secretive, extremely secretive character.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you a clarification of something you just said above. That's at our temporary transcript page 34, line 19. You said: "However, during those three years of education at location 1, there have never been actions by instructors or management personnel, the likes of which occurred within the unit." Could you explain what you meant when you said that?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Specifically what I meant by this is this: No instructions or professors at location 1 stated, I'm trying to quote their words, one of commanders at one occasion said, If any of you does not do as told by me, I can kill that person at this moment and to write on his grave he bravely gave his life to the fatherland. And this prompted me and my colleagues to doubt and to be afraid, sort of.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: You feel comfortable telling us the name of who said that in open session, or would you prefer in private session?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: I would prefer for that to be in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: JF-048, can you describe the supply warehouse at location 2. What kinds of supplies were there?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: The warehouse itself was located close to the entrance to the camp. The warehouse was a low building connected with the dining room, meaning the kitchen and the dining room, the mess room. When we first arrived at location 2, we were issued with everything that we needed for the training; weapons, the uniforms. And at the back of the warehouse, if I remember correctly, there was a section for storing food. In the rest of the warehouse was stockpiled were ammunition, uniforms, and all other supplies that we needed for training.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: How would you compare the kinds of supplies which were kept and distributed at location 2 with those at the other locations?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: What was interesting is that supplies, if we can call them that, at location 4 and those at location 2 -- well, location 2 supplies were of a character corresponded to the current needs of the unit. As I said, uniforms, food, ammunition, weapons. Whereas at location 4, in certain facilities, there were everything, to put it simply. Everything was warehoused there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'm going to return that in just a few minutes when we talk about location 4. Now during your time - we are still talking about location 2 - did you come to know the connection or relationship, if any, between Arkan's Men and the DB?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: The only thing that I can state in respect of the relationship between Red Berets or the JATD and Arkan's Tigers and later on the Boca unit, is that on two occasions I saw members of Arkan's Tigers coming to location 2 to fetch supplies. I specifically saw them stacking green coloured crates, military crates, as I presumed because I wasn't close enough to see accurately what was in them, but those were military type crates for ammunition or hand-grenades. On another occasion, two or three members -- I'm sorry, I don't know exactly how many. Those were from the Boca unit coming there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'll ask you about Boca's unit in just a moment. Staying with Arkan's Tigers, what was your understanding of how it was that Arkan's Tigers could obtain supplies from the DB camp?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: How was that possible is not something I could divine from my position, neither did I try to divine that. It was a public secret, so to speak, that Arkan's Tigers were no official unit of the Ministry of the Interior, whereas, it was known in respect of us that we were members of a special unit of the state security sector. How those two units were connected is not something I can explain. I can just state what I saw at location 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, returning to what you said about Boca's detachment. You talk about this on page 10 in your statement. Can you provide any greater detail as to what kind of supplies Boca's detachment obtained from the warehouse at location 2 to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: As far as I know on both occasions in the case when I saw Arkan's Tigers members and members of the Boca detachment, in both cases those crates were green, military-type crates, which most probably contained ammunition or hand-grenades. Military equipment or military supplies at any rate.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately when it was that you saw Boca's detachment? The month is fine.

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection that could only have been in either July or August 1995. I think there's more of a chance that it was actually July, at least that's what I can remember now because it's been a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: At the time did you know who Boca's detachment was?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: I had no information about what sort of a detachment it was. I could only see what I did see, and this was news to me. One of my presumptions was that it was one of the, well, let's call them special units, but I had never heard or known of this unit before. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, moving on to location 3. At location 3 did you have the same instructors as you had at location 2?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Most of them were the same, plus there may have been a couple of new instructors. What I knew at the time was that they came from another unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: JF-048, how would you compare the kinds of supplies which were kept and distributed at location 3 with the other locations?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: In essence at location 3, this was a ready-made or a makeshift camp. There were no solid buildings there. Mostly they were tents. At location 3 in addition to the tents where we slept there was another tent with a smaller number of ammunition crates and a small amount of food, 99 per cent of which was canned food.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you see Franko Simatovic at location 3?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: At location 3, I never saw Mr. Frenki Simatovic there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, moving on to location 4, were there any other groups present at location 4 apart from your group?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: As for location 4, when I just arrived there, there was the Poskok unit. As far as I remember, my unit and the Poskok unit merged around that time. They also used the location number 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What did you do during your time at location 4?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: On both tours at location 4 as far as I remember -- well, that location did not offer such possibilities as locations 2 or even more location 5. What should I call it? It was a temporary holding area of sorts to move on to another, say, X location.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I just want to clarify, the question I asked you was in relation to location 4. I just want to be sure that that was your answer for location 4. It can be a little bit confusing since we are not using the names of the places. My question was what you did during your time at location 4?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Well, to tell you the truth, it is a bit confusing with the numbers. But as I've said already, I may have omitted to say that at location 4 one could, and we did, undertake only basic physical training. We had sufficient space for that. These included morning warmup, exercises in the field in front of the main building, but such training as there was at locations 1, 3, and 5 is something we did not do at location 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to ask you just a few more questions about location 4 since you didn't elaborate as much in your statement on that location. Could you compare the kinds of supplies which were kept and distributed at location 4 with other locations. You stated to tell us about it a little bit earlier, perhaps you can elaborate on that.

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Yes, there was something specific concerning location 4 and I saw this myself, and it was absent in all other locations, was that close to the main building where the unit was, as far as I recall, there were three or four large hangars. Well, I won't enumerate everything, but there were enormous quantities of foreign produced cigarettes to luxurious foreign cars. I even saw an American ambulance in one of the hangars and on location 4 I even saw foreign combat vehicles. I remember clearly there was a French combat vehicle there in addition to a few others.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What uniforms did you wear during your time in training at location 4?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: As far as I recall we wore NATO uniforms. That is to say camouflage uniforms with the pattern resembling NATO uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And what insignias, if any, did you wear at location 4?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: As far as I recall, we had the Red Berets with the wolf emblem or patch, and as far as I recall it wasn't desirable to sport any kind of insignia on the uniform itself. If I'm not mistaken, we did not have any insignia on the uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you recall what insignias were worn by your instructors at location 4?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you recall any insignias worn by your commanders at location 4?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Unfortunately I really cannot recall that. Anything I might say would be speculation. I don't want to tell you anything I cannot remember with certainty.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could we have private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'm going to turn now to location 5. How would you compare the kinds of supplies which were kept and distributed at location 5 with the other locations?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: The supplies at location 5 in essence -- well, there is one way to compare the locations. It is my conclusion that the other locations save for locations 1 and 5 were temporary locations. Whereas location 5 following my arrival there -- well, we were told that it was to be our permanent location. Of course, the supplies at that location especially in terms of food and conditions were far better than at other locations.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Were there any other groups present at location 5 apart from your group?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: No. As I've stated already, it was around that time as far as I remember, our unit, the JATD, merged, or rather, took in members of the Poskok unit of the Krajina. If you had in mind such units which I was able to observe at location 2, then I can tell you that they were not present at location 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What did you do during your time at location 5?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: At location 5 as in the case of locations 1 and 3, we underwent physical and combat training plus theory, plus martial arts training because the conditions were far better. We also had our regular duties befalling any member of the unit at my level, i.e., standing guard, being on duty during the night and day.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, we've been through the five locations, four of which were -- have been camps that you are talking about. Can you compare for us what you knew about the JATD, the Red Berets, the group you had joined, what you knew at location 2 with what your understanding and perception was by the time you reached location 5?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: I apologise, I did not understand exactly. What location did you refer to, was it location 2?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, I'm trying to compare what your perception was of the unit from the beginning, from the first location which is location 2 being the first camp, comparing that with what your perception was of the unit at location 5. Some time had passed, these locations go chronologically, so I'm trying to understand if your perception had changed in any way, and if so, in what way did your perception and understanding change?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Of course it changed drastically. Following location 2 and up to location 5, the simplest explanation or an answer to your question would be this: While I was at location 2, I did understand that it was a special unit, that we were to undergo rigorous training, and that discipline was required. This is something that applied to all the locations. But having graduated to location 5 with time I came to realize that that location was an official location for a respectable unit. That's at least my opinion, my view of things. For example, at location 2 as well as at location 3, there were a few cases, which in my view having learned what I did at location 1, would have otherwise been impermissible within the MUP. At location 5, however, at least to my knowledge, such things did not happen.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Was there any kind of psychological training which you underwent at any time in any of these locations?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: In my view we were exposed to some sort of psychological training on a daily basis, starting with the very banal fact such as hearing your instructor say every day that he was both your mother and father at the same time and everything that matters to you in the whole world up to certain types of training and types of punishment even. In my view, we were exposed to daily psychological training of some sort. The gist of that type of training, in my view, was to realise the importance of the unit, the importance of secrecy within that unit, and the importance of obeying what one is told under any circumstances. We were not to ponder on the rights and wrongs of something. We would simply hear instructors say, this is it, and that's your whole story.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you have any kind of oath or pledge which you took as part of the JATD Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: In terms of an official oath such as an oath that would be taken before a court, that did not exist. However, there was an oath well known amongst us. I cannot recall the exact words now, but it boils down to -- well, I'm explaining the meaning of it. It boiled down to if you were ever left alone in the field during an operation, take great care not to fall into enemy hands alive. You put a bull let through your brain, but do not allow yourself to be taken alive. I think that would be the right answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'm going to ask our Case Manager to play a clip from the unit video, part 2. It's been uploaded at 65 ter 2609.3. It corresponds to the full video which is 2609 at 42 minutes, 57 seconds to 43 minutes 35 seconds. I'd like to just note that when this was reviewed it turned out that the transcript did not have this particular portion in it. We noticed that in the English. We immediately submitted it for translation, and now we are going to upload the full English translation for the full transcript. In the meantime, the transcript will run underneath it as we play it, and the booth has been given the translation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "One day when you find yourself alone in the battle-field." Interpreter's note: We cannot make out the text, we can merely follow the subtitles. [Voiceover] And the enemy women, children, and dogs came to tear you to pieces, shoot a bullet through your head and die a hero."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus, apparently the sound was such that the interpreters could not translate from the original words spoken. If there's any challenge to what is said and whether it's accurately translated, then I'm primarily addressing native speaking persons or those who have access to native speaking persons. Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the sound was very bad and in Serbian I basically understood nothing. Therefore, I have full understanding for the interpreters. One simply cannot make anything out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the question remains whether this is -- what the probative value is. Apparently someone once thought that he could hear what was said. I would suggest that if there are any -- even if a repeated effort is made, if there's still no possibility to hear what was said in the original language, then of course, we'd have to consider that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'd just like to note, during preparation the witness told me what the oath was and then upon watching this later, he started reciting it while it was going on. So this is the reason for showing it now. The witness can certainly comment on it. He could even sing it along with the participants if Your Honours prefer so that the words can be translated by the interpreters simultaneously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Whether he would then -- if you can't hear what is said in the original language then it may be difficult to conclude that the witness is using the same words as the words which could not be heard, but he suggests are used. I would, as a matter of fact -- I would suggest that the parties try again to see whether -- or to hear whether they can come to a similar conclusion as the Prosecution. If not, then I'd like to hear from the Defence, and we could ask perhaps others to advise us on the matter. Now, whatever is said, whether they say anything or not, it's what the witness apparently testified. So even without the video, that testimony stands, and I do understand you well that he first spoke those words when being interviewed himself and only after that you had showed him the video. The one question remains, had you seen this video before, Witness JF-048?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had seen this footage before. However, I want to say that I saw this oath in written form for the first time at location 2. It was in a notepad belonging to one of my instructors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, when you watched this video, did you listen to the original language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And did you recognise the words spoken or almost shouted to be the same words as you learned to be the kind of pledge or what you earlier told us? Were you able to understand what they said or what they shouted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, especially in the part of the video where the unit members take the oath just before lunch. The second part where the oath is spoken by I believe what are Arkan's Tigers, this is something I saw for the first time on TV. However, the other part of the footage showing members of my former unit just before lunch, that is something I am familiar with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and you did hear them use the words you know as what we call the -- well, it's not a real oath, but at least the pledge, shoot yourself rather than to fall into the hands of the enemy? Could you recognise the words?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you now remember the precise text? Could you speak it, could you tell us aloud what the exact wording is, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One day when you are left wounded in the battle-field and enemy women, children, and dogs arrive -- I apologise, this is a bit stressful for me. So enemy, women, children, and dogs arrive to tear you apart, put a bullet through your head and die a hero.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: JF-048, the video we have just seen, was this members of your unit or members of Arkan's Tigers?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: No, the people in black uniforms, at least during the period I was with the unit, did not exist in that unit. These were Arkan's Tigers. In the other portion of the footage where you can see guys in NATO uniforms, these would be members of my unit. Or rather, of the unit I was a member of.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, what I would propose with your leave is to mark this clip for identification and then to submit it for, I guess, an official translation. Maybe the experts in the Registry who do the translation will be able to determine whether it's audible or inaudible. We note that there was no notation in the transcript saying words inaudible which usually does appear in an official translation and then perhaps we can tender it into evidence at that stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash or Mr. Petrovic, any comment on this suggestion by Ms. Marcus to have it marked for identification so that everyone can give it another try to see whether they can identify the words spoken or used?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, that's -- could I just seek clarification. This seems to be a new element to the Prosecution case. Is it their case that this is a pledge taken by everybody who joined the Serbian DB's Red Beret unit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I fully endorse this approach. However, some words are intelligible but it is not clear whether those both groups that could be seen are uttering those words or not. This could not be concluded from the video footage, and what is unclear also is how this was edited and who compiled the whole video footage that we saw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, could you tell us of which portion you understood what words so that we can better focus. The black uniforms or the ones sitting at the table, which ones were you able to --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have to be frank, I cannot pinpoint which words I could understand. I would have to redo it and listen to it very carefully to inform you. I can do it later in the day or tomorrow and let you know. I had an impression that the people are not mouthing in sync with the audio because what we could see were two groups of people saying something, and the audio seemed to be one. I could understand a word or two out of the whole melee, the sound was very poor, but if we were to hear it in better audio conditions, maybe we could understand more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's appreciated that you want to give it another try. Could you already tell us what words you thought you had understood? The word or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For instance, Your Honour, I think I understood women and children, but if you give me some time, I will seriously deal with it, otherwise it would be hardly of any assistance if I were to try to explain which words. I did, however, understand some words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrovic, the reason why I asked you this is, and of course, as I said before, we appreciate that you want to give it another try, if you would have understood words which do not appear in what is now the transcript then of course we might have a more serious problem compared to the situation where the words you just mentioned are at least in the text which we have seen recently. Mr. Registrar, the MFI number for this clip of this video.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The Exhibit will be P535 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Witness JF-048, could you tell us --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, I don't know if Your Honours ruled against me in terms of seeking clarification on the issue. It just would be nice to know if that's the Prosecution case before the translation of the video comes out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let me -- that is a question. I understood, but perhaps I'm wrong, therefore perhaps we just ask the witness, is that this was a kind of a repeated kind of yell with a special meaning for and not something to be officially taken at joining the unit. Is that correctly understood, Witness JF-048, that you would on a regular basis now and then yell as a group those words? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you are right, Your Honour. Those words or this recital was done by us before taking a meal. We never officially took a pledge having such words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus, is what the witness just said, does that fit into the Prosecution's case?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The use of the word "oath" was the terminology that was used by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jordash, is that sufficiently clear?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could the Court Officer please call up 65 ter 5358. I note that this is the first chart that is in the hard copy handouts that we've provided to all the parties and to the Chamber. 5358. It is a payment list authentication spreadsheet. Please, may I ask not to broadcast it. May I ask that the English be shown although there is obviously a B/C/S version. The witness understands English quite well, and I think it would be more visible to everybody if we could show the English version. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: JF-048, in preparation for your testimony in this case, you were asked to review a number of payment records and provide your comments upon them. Did you, in fact, review a number of payment records, the ones listed in this chart, and did you comment upon them?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Were you given an opportunity to review what was written to ensure it was accurate according to the information you had provided?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could I please ask to show the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Is this your signature which appears at the bottom of this spreadsheet?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Yes, that's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to tender this authentication chart into evidence. It's 65 ter 5358 under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. Mr. Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number would be P536 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P536 is admitted into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: How would you compare the payments you received with payments you might receive performing the normal job of a police officer?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: I think that I've already stated, particularly at location number 2, the salary was given in cash without any administrative procedures, no chits being signed, no decisions on the level of pay, and to the best of my recollection, that those administrative procedures took place at location 5, and then from that point onwards, we received our salaries just as any other officers in an envelope with a letterhead of MUP and with signing that we had received our salaries.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: How would you compare the quantity that you were paid, the amount of your salary in the unit with the amount of a salary you would have received as an ordinary police officer?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Well, our salary in the unit were drastically higher that the take-home pay of members of public security, I mean policemen. They were drastically higher. And for the conditions of the time in the area of former Yugoslavia, our salaries were quite high. Our salaries.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you recall any occasions when the payments that you received varied in quantity and amount when you received a different amount?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: I cannot recall the specific amounts to the dinar, but there were occasions once or twice that on top of salary we would receive bonuses or a premium over salary. We called them premiums.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you recall what circumstances led to you receiving a bonus or a premium over your salary?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, there was no particular reason. But if my memory serves me well, this mostly used to happen after our stay at location 3, for instance. When we would be at location 3, if I remember correctly, we would receive those premiums. My conclusion was that those premiums were connected with us being at that location and not at our regular location. In MUP we used to call them, at least in public security sector, as an allowance for a stay in the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could the Court Officer please call up 65 ter 5359, which is also in the hard copy handouts that have been given to the parties. Similar to the previous one this one is in English and B/C/S in e-court, but if we can show the English so that the witness can confirm it, that should be good.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: JF-048, in preparation for your testimony in this case, you were asked to review your own DB personnel file and provide comments upon each document contained therein. Did you, in fact, conduct this review of the documents listed on this chart and did you comment upon them?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: I apologise, yes, I did review those documents and I commented on them. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Sorry, is it possible to see the English version. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Were you given an opportunity to review what was written when you gave your comments to ensure it was accurate according to the information that you had provided?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Yes. This confirms the information contained in the original documents, yes. Or the documents that I saw written in the Serbian language.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Just to verify, this is not being broadcast, is that correct? I'm sorry, I didn't ask for it. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Is this your signature which appears on the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Yes, that's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to tender this authentication chart into evidence. It is 65 ter 5359 under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. Mr. Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number would be Exhibit P537 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P537 is admitted under seal. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, again I note the time, if Your Honours would like me to continue I can, or we can take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time would you still need, Ms. Marcus?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Well, I guess it depends on the objection, but if there are no objections very briefly, maybe ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, of course, I'm not asking the parties whether they will object to any question which is difficult to forecast. We resumed effectively, at least on this clock, at ten minutes past 5.00. This is the usual time for a break, but I can imagine that the parties would prefer to hear the last ten minutes of examination-in-chief first. I'm also looking at Mr. Stanisic. We can take a break without any problem, but Mr. Jordash, if you --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'll just take instructions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: May we have a break now, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll have a break now and we will resume at five minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank, Your Honour. Could I ask the Court Officer to please call up 65 ter 5360, not to broadcast it to the public, please. This is third chart that is in the hard-copy handouts provided to all present. I'd like to note for the record that this chart is identified as 65 ter 1167 which is actually an exhibit marked for identification that is P395 MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: JF-048, in preparation for your testimony today, did you watch the Skorpions video and comment upon it to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: There's no sound coming from the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we check whether the witness's microphone is switched on. Could you please repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did watch the video and I provided some comments on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Were your comments noted down in the chart we see before us?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Yes, these are my comments that I provided after watching the video.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Were you given an opportunity to review what was written to ensure it was accurate according to the information you provided?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This is exactly what I did once again.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Perhaps we could scroll down to the bottom of the page in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Is this your signature which appears on the bottom of this chart?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Yes, this is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time I would tender this spreadsheet into evidence under seal. It is 65 ter 5360.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of -- yes, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, our objection would refer to the fact that those -- this video footage dates from June 1995. I do not recall witness stating that he saw anything of the sort in June 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: On the contrary, the witness testified that he believes that he saw Boca's detachment at location 2 in June or July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems that he stated July or August, but this is very easily verifiable, if I'm wrong. But I do believe he has stated July or August.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I apologise, at page 40, lines 20 through 23, what the witness said is: "To the best of my recollection that could only have been in either July or August 1995. I think there's more of a chance that it was actually July. At least that's what I can remember now, because it's been a long time ago."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and Mr. Petrovic said that he had not seen anything from June, which is then --

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, if you look at the witness's comments, he is saying this is the type of vehicle, this is the insignia I saw, and those are the type of crates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's a different matter which apparently is not covered. The comments are of a kind that the witness identifies the persons he sees and sometimes describes what the functions were and his comment on, for example, vehicles is not that he saw this at this very moment, but he is testifying or at least is giving his comments as to his familiarity with the type of documents. Mr. Petrovic. Mr. Jordash, any comments?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is overruled. Mr. Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number would be P538 under seal, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P538 is admitted into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could the Court Officer now please call up 65 ter 5361 and again not broadcast it to the public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By the way, I'm mixed up as a matter of fact in my previous comments, the recognition of persons with -- because that was not what was on our screen. Yes, I was already going too fast and said that the witness recognised persons, but then I was apparently referring to this series of stills from the Kula camp video. I apologise for that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: JF-048, in preparation for your testimony today did you watch the Kula camp video and comment upon it to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Yes, I did watch the video and provided my comments on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Were your comments noted down in the chart we see before us?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Could you please zoom in on the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I think again perhaps if we show the English version, that would suffice.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, these are my comments.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Were you given an opportunity to review what was written to ensure it was accurate according to the information you provided?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Is this your signature we see at the bottom of each page of this chart?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Yes, at the bottom of this document is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you one clarification. In the bottom photo that you see on the screen in front of you, at the timing 1 minute 28 seconds, you say this is Zvezdan Jovanovic, aka Zveki. Can you tell us whether your comment refers to the man on the left or the man on the right?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: My remark refers to the person on the right-hand side so the first person from the right is him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time I would tender this spreadsheet into evidence under seal. It is 65 ter 5361.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections? Mr. Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P539 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P539 is admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: JF-048, I have one final question for you. On today's transcript on page 57, lines 5 through 7, I'm going to quote to you what you said and just ask you for a clarification. You said: "I cannot recall the specific amounts to the dinar but there were occasions once or twice that on top of salary we would receive bonuses or a premium over salary. We called them premiums." Apart from the salary and bonuses once or twice which you received, did you receive any other payments when you were part of the unit?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time I would like to tender the underlying payment records authenticated by the witness. I can read the numbers into the record or I could provide them as Your Honours please afterwards to the Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How many numbers would have to be reserved for that purpose, or is it one number?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I will tell you just now. It's eight numbers, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Eight numbers. Mr. Registrar, could you already tell us what the numbers would be that you would reserve.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit P540 up to Exhibit P547, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is this all for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Those are the payment records that the witness authenticated, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections? Not. Then P540 up to and including P547 are admitted into evidence under seal. If you would give a table for the Registrar which exactly are the numbers, the corresponding numbers and the corresponding descriptions of the documents, if there's any problem with the description, then I would say by Thursday we would hear those objections, and if not, we'll accept your description as given to the Registrar. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We will do so. Finally, I would also like to tender from the bar table the DB personnel file for this witness. It was provisionally assigned 65 ter 5344. I note that it is not on our 65 ter list, Your Honours, and we received it pursuant to RFA 1691 from BIA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When did you receive it?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: We received it in September of 2008, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections against?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then in the absence of any objections, Mr. Registrar, the Exhibit number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P548, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P548 is admitted into evidence under seal. Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm done with my examination-in-chief. I just have one final comment I'd like to put on the record with your leave. The Prosecution disputes Mr. Petrovic's submission in relation to the clip which has now been marked as P535 marked for identification that this is a voice-over of a clip. It's for the Trial Chamber -- we submit that it's for the Trial Chamber to determine to watch it again and make its determination of whether the Trial Chamber considers it to be a voice-over, and certainly if the Chamber so requests, the Prosecution is prepared to conduct a forensic examination to reach a resolution of this issue. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From what I understood is that -- I understood that Mr. Petrovic will have a closer look at the document and then I take it that he will include in his review of the video whether there's any voice-over or whether it's -- we hear the voice of at least a voice which corresponds with the lip movements of the person. We'll hear then further from Mr. Petrovic. My usual question is who is going to cross-examine the witness first. I noticed that over time the Simatovic Defence has found itself sometimes some trouble at the end in being urged to see whether we could finish the witness, but I leave it to the parties whether the sequence is as often Stanisic first and then Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It is us again, but we do discuss it with our learned friends and make our decisions accordingly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and, Witness JF-048, you'll now be

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Whilst you were at location 1 did you commit -- you personally commit any crimes?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Same question location 2, did you commit any crimes at location 2?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Location 3, did you personally commit any crimes?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Location 4, same question, please.

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And location 5, did you commit any crimes?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: In location 2 did your unit commit any crimes whilst you were there?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Same question location 3, did your unit commit any crimes whilst present in that location?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: The same answer to the best of my knowledge, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And would you give the same answer to the same question in relation to location 4, did your unit commit any crimes?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: The same answer goes to location 4 and location 5, as I say to the best of my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. And is it right that at none of those locations were you given any orders to commit any crimes? Is that correct also?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: At no location did I receive any orders that I was supposed to commit any crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, can I take you to the beginning of your evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we please go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have the English one, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Would you have a look at the B/C/S while that's happening, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, I think we've got the wrong -- either I misspoke or it was trans -- anyway, it's 4175, and I think we've got 4715 on the screen. I don't know if I misspoke or what, but I don't suppose it matters. 4175, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, is this what you want to have on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Have you had the opportunity to read that, Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: I'm reading it right now. Are you asking me whether I have seen it before?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm -- what I'm asking you is whether the Alfa camp that you were told about is this Alfa camp mentioned in this military document as opening in June of 1993? Is that what you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: I have no information about the establishment of Alfa camp. I just heard my instructor referring to that camp, and the camp was supposedly near Knin. As for any dates of when it was established or any other information, well, that's something I don't have.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I can leave the subject with this question: The origin of the unit as far as you understood whilst you were at location 2 and afterwards throughout your time with the unit was that it started in a camp called the Alfa camp; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: That is what our instructor said when he referred to the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And you never heard anything during your time with the unit which suggested different to that, that it had other origins; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: I never heard any other information. In essence, what is at hand here is that I heard my immediate superior say that our initial instructors had been trained at the Alfa camp, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, I just want to be clear about this. Your initial instructors had been trained at the Alfa camp and they were the origins of the unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: May I tender this from the bar table, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number would be Exhibit D71, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D71 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have, please, back on the screen, P523. And can we go to page 6 of the English and the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I take you to paragraph 4 of the B/C/S and also page 4 of the English. The paragraph I'm interested in is the paragraph where it says: "A Krajina-based unit known as Poskok also functioned in the RSK as did the Red Berets. Members of this Poskok unit appear to have been trained at the aforementioned Alfa centre and they were seasoned soldiers." You see that? "Milos Opacic commanded the Poskok unit when I met them in late 1995 but members of this unit were eventually absorbed into the Red Berets by 1996." You see that?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: I can't locate that paragraph, what does it start with? I'm looking at the Serbian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think it should be page 6 of the Serbian and page 6 of the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Starting with the words "RSK and the Red Berets?"

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry, not starting with the words RSK but starting with "a Krajina-based unit known as Poskok..."

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: I can see the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
