utterances.text: The Poskok unit, as noted here, you say, were -- let me start that again. In what way do you suggest the Poskok unit was absorbed into the Red Berets by 1996? Can you explain how this occurred, if you know?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: I'll tell you what I remember. When my part of the unit was at location 4, the aforementioned unit Poskok arrived. We shared the same camp, the same dormitories. We took meals together and they stayed there with us for awhile.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But they were operating as a separate unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Specifically they never operated together with us only. At location 3, two or three of our men came to us and one of them was a personal instructor of mine. They later on followed us to location 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The man Milos Opacic, did he ever join the Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: I remember him specifically from a conversation we had at location 4. He showed me some pictures. There was something specific about him in the sense that he liked listening to the Beethoven's 9th when going into action. And at that moment in time, we shared location 4 with him.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Beethoven's 8th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To tell you the truth, however, I cannot recall him being at location 5, but I do recall the other two or three members of that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did Milos Opacic join the Red Berets at any time?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that, but I do know, as I said already, that he was in the same camp at location 4 where we were at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And you were at location 4 for how long, with Opacic?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: I was at location 4 on two occasions, if I remember it correctly. He was there when I was at location 4 for the first time. My part of the unit spent a bit less than a month there, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me try to shortcut this.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can we have on e-court, please, P539.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can I just ask to make sure it's not broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, yes. Can we go to page 2. Could we also have the B/C/S up on the screen for my client. Page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And the bit I'm interested in while the B/C/S is coming up is 959 where you make the comment: "This is one of the Opacic brothers, he used to be a member of the Poskok unit, but on this video he is a member of the Red Berets. His brother was with me at location 4."

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What did you mean by "but on this video he is a member of the Red Berets?"

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: According to my information they were from another unit, from the Poskok unit. However, on this footage we see Mr. Opacic in a Red Beret uniform, filed alongside some Red Beret veterans. I don't know him personally, but as I've already said, I saw him brother at location 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. So when you watched the video, am I correct that you were surprised when you heard him described as a veteran of the special unit of the state security because it was your experience that he was none of the sort; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: Could you please reformulate your question. I failed to understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: All right. From what you saw and heard in your time in the unit Opacic was not a member of the Red Berets, he was a member of the Poskok unit; correct?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: I said that about his brother and not about the gentleman we see in the still.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, the gentleman in the still, you made a comment on the chart expressing surprise that he was a Red Beret, is that correct, or he was portrayed as a Red Beret in the Kula award ceremony?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness never said on the chart anything about surprise.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, I'm obviously putting an interpretation on it, I'm asking the witness if he accepts that. I can reformulate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps if the witness had already some difficulties with your previous question and I -- if the witness would not have expressed it, I might have said something about it. Could you please try to clearly distinguish between facts and emotional experience.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: When you said, Mr. Witness, in the chart about Opacic brother, he used to be a member of the Poskok unit but on this video, he is a member of the Red Berets, you were expressing surprise because it was your experience that Opacic was not a Red Beret; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: I wasn't surprised. I merely watched the footage and I heard the officers introduce themselves to Slobodan Milosevic. This gentleman said, Opacic, I forget the first name, and then it came to me that this was Opacic's brother and now I see him in the Red Berets. When I discussed this with Opacic, I believe he told me they were members of the Poskok unit. That's all I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'll leave it at that. Yes, I'll leave it at that. Thank you. Well, with one question. You had not heard or seen anything which suggested that Opacic was a member of the Red Beret unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JF-048
utterances.text: If you have Milos Opacic in mind, the person I was at location 4 with, at that time he was a Poskok member but the unit was in the same camp where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. We can leave it there. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can we go back, please, to P523 on e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not to be shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Not to be shown, Your Honour, thank you. Actually, sorry, let me deal with something else. Please can I have on the screen P540.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, I take it that you made a calculated guess which document finally would end up under 540 which is in the range of where the descriptions still are to be expected.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm hoping.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but Mr. Registrar reserved the numbers but is still waiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Perhaps the easiest way to do it is to go to 65 ter 5358, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is the chart.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It's the chart. 65 ter 5358.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Not to be shown to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Looking, Mr. Witness, at the names you've identified here as those that you recognise, would you agree with me that all of these named persons you recognise received, from what you saw, professional training, professional police training whilst at the school at location 1?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, perhaps my colleague could clarify what he is talking about in terms of all these named persons. Because the witness talks about a lot of different people in the explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, what I understand Mr. Jordash would like to find out whether all these names on the list were with the witness at that location, is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you rephrase it so that everyone understands the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Perhaps we should go into private session, if we can so I can ask the question with freedom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. We adjourn for the day and we will resume tomorrow, Wednesday the 16th of June, quarter past 2.00 in this same Courtroom II.
